To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) integrated behavioral health care in primary care is feasible and can be effective, (2) integrated behavioral care is a complex process that is not easily achieved, (3) training of primary care providers in integrated behavioral health care is feasible and effective, but requires a high level of support from the residency and medical center, and (4) training of behavioral health providers in integrated care is feasible, effective and requires the same level of support as training primary care providers.
the training of integrated behavioral health providers is feasible and that prescribing psychologists have a unique role to play in integrated primary care.

integrated training of primary health care providers, prescribing psychologists, behavioral specialists, and behavioral health consultants is feasible, but that the barriers and solutions to integrated training are complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the delivery and training of integrated behavioral care in a primary care setting.
how to best train family physicians, prescribing psychologists and psychological/behavior consultants in integrated care.
the development, evaluation, and dissemination of evidence-based, integrated behavioral care training for family physicians and prescribing psychologists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
integrated behavioral health training in primary care residency is a valuable and feasible endeavor.
the training of family practice physicians, prescribing psychologists (and other behavioral specialists) in integrated behavioral care is a complex, but worthwhile, endeavor.
integrated training of primary-care physicians, prescribing psychologists and other behavioral specialists is possible and valuable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective model of training family physicians, prescribing psychologists and behavioral health consultants in integrated behavioral care.

integrated training of family practice physicians and prescribing psychologists in integrated behavioral care is feasible, but requires significant commitment of faculty and staff time, as well as financial support.
we have developed an integrated training model in a family practice residency, with the family medicine resident and the prescribing psychologist as central figures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
training in integrated care can be accomplished in a primary care residency, and the authors offer a model for such training that includes the role of prescribing psychologists.
training programs that prepare psychologists to work in primary care can be successful.
training programs can be developed that train all members of the integrated care team, including family physicians, prescribing psychologists and behavioral health consultants.
